cards.front: Recall a key point about Athenian Daily Life & Society
cards.back: The oikos (household) was the basic social unit: the male head (kyrios) controlled the family, property and dependants

cards.front: Recall a key point about Athenian Daily Life & Society
cards.back: Athenian women lived largely secluded lives in the women's quarters (gynaikeion); they could not vote, own property or conduct business independently

cards.front: Recall a key point about Athenian Daily Life & Society
cards.back: The symposium was an elite male drinking party featuring conversation, music and entertainment; it was central to aristocratic social and political networking

cards.front: Recall a key point about Athenian Daily Life & Society
cards.back: Slavery was fundamental to the Athenian economy: slaves worked in homes, workshops, mines and fields; they had no legal rights

cards.front: Recall a key point about Athenian Daily Life & Society
cards.back: Education (paideia) for boys focused on grammar, music and physical training; girls received little or no formal education

cards.front: Recall a key point about Athenian Daily Life & Society
cards.back: Hetairai (courtesans) were educated women who attended symposia and had more freedom than citizen wives

cards.back: 1. For Athenian Daily Life & Society, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2.
